title: When an ant takes a fruit, where should the seed inside end up?
question: Today the seed dies the moment an ant picks the fruit up. Two ways to let it live. (1) ON THE SPOT: the ant eats the flesh and leaves the pip lying where it bit, so the seed survives but hardly moves. (2) CARRIED HOME: the seed rides inside the ant and is put down wherever that ant puts things down - which for a laden ant is mostly the nest, so you get a ring of herbs around the nest and a bed whose planting map is a record of where the colony foraged. Which is the one you want to watch, and is (2) worth roughly three times the work?
context_md:
Your played bed at 40,000 frames: the nest band is the pale strip in the middle, plants either side. In this box a colony takes about **2,300 mouthfuls and gets 62 of them home**, and a fruit is the richest thing on the ground it can find. Every one of those seeds is currently destroyed on pickup.

**What (2) gives you that (1) does not** is the headline: a line of ants carrying fruit home, and then a stand of herbs growing out of the midden. The colony becomes the plants' delivery service and the plants become a larder that refills itself - which is the direct answer to your own "over a long enough time everything dies out".

**What (1) gives you** is the same rule at a third of the cost and no new state anywhere: a fruit eaten leaves a seed behind instead of a hole. It stops the colony being a pure seed sink, and it is nearly invisible.

Either way the seed will not always survive - that is a number on the plant you can turn, so a fruit going through an animal is a gamble rather than a guarantee.

Nothing here is built. This decides which one gets built first.

items.caption: Played bed, frame 40,000. The nest is the bare strip at soil level in the middle.
